source.title: Towards Unifying Interpretability and Control: Evaluation via Intervention
source.authors: Usha Bhalla; Suraj Srinivas; Asma Ghandeharioun; Himabindu Lakkaraju

record.tranche_reason: Tests the causal fidelity and reconstruction of SAE features, and reports incomplete reconstruction and inconsistent feature-to-output effects that qualify claims about SAE features as complete, reliable representational units. It does not test superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates interventions through SAE features, but does not test whether models with more sparse features than dimensions represent them as overlapping directions, nor whether LLM activations are distributed across neurons. Only SAE reconstruction and intervention outcomes relevant to feature completeness or causal fidelity are included. Other intervention methods and prompting results are not findings about SAE features as model units.
record.test_reason: The study is mainly a steering benchmark. Only its SAE reconstruction error (Appendix A.1) bears directly on V5's completeness part. The SAE intervention results test auto-interpreted feature labels as steering handles, not whether SAE features are the model's units. It is a weak test of V5 completeness only.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but slightly overstated. The authors conclude that current interpretability methods allow intervention but inconsistently across features and models. Lens methods beat SAEs and probes on simple concrete features, with SAE shortfalls attributed to erroneous post-hoc labels. Mechanistic interventions trade off coherence and underperform prompting, and explanations are 'less accurate than expected'. They do not frame the results as evidence about whether SAE features are the model's representational units.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates intervention through SAE, lens, probe, steering-vector, and prompting methods; it does not reproduce the original Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Intervention efficacy varies with intervention strength and model; Appendix A.4 reports layer-dependent effects for GPT2-small, with later layers more effective for Logit Lens and Tuned Lens.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering via auto-labelled SAE features needs larger edits and succeeds less often than logit or tuned lens. SAE token probabilities sit around 1e-5 versus 1e-4 to 0.5 for other methods. The authors blame noisy feature labels, e.g. a 'coffee' feature that also encodes 'beans'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Auto-interpreted SAE feature labels are unreliable handles for causal steering, compared with lens-based features.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE intervention directions are near-orthogonal to Logit and Tuned Lens directions and closer to steering and probe directions, even when all succeed (Fig. 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different interpretability methods' edit directions for the same concept do not coincide.

record.problems: Relevant SAE intervention outcomes are mostly presented as plots without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The study tests selected features and topics, not SAE feature stability or canonicality.
record.rows_left_out: No other relevant SAE reconstruction or intervention results were omitted. Figure 4's complex-feature comparisons do not report a sufficiently specific SAE outcome in the text to add a separate model-by-feature row.

untested.parts: Stability of features across seeds or sizes, canonicality, and whether SAE features are the model's own computational units. The study uses only pretrained SAEs (SAELens, Gemma Scope) at single layers. Completeness is tested only via reconstruction error on GPT2-small L9 and Gemma2-2b L20; there is no SAE reconstruction figure for Llama models.
Not tested; pretrained SAEs are used as tools.

missing.what: Coherence of outputs when activations are replaced by their SAE reconstructions without intervention; the paper says it generally matches clean coherence. This bears on the functional completeness of SAE reconstructions.

record.verdict_notes: SAE results come from pretrained third-party SAEs selected via Neuronpedia labels, with some topics mapped to imperfect features. The study is primarily about steering utility, so its bearing on superposition is limited to V5 completeness via reconstruction error. The GPT2-small error above 1 is suspicious.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise from competition for limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Whether features are distributed across multiple neurons or whether SAEs recover known sparse features in LLMs.

The study tests SAE feature reconstruction and causal fidelity for selected interventions, but not feature stability across settings or whether SAE features are canonical units of model representation.
Whether the features represented by the tested methods are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Measured normalized latent reconstruction error for SAE reconstruction without intervention.
rows.note: The error indicates reconstruction is not exact; the paper does not give a threshold for completeness.
rows.check: Fine as a completeness measure (Gemma Scope SAE, layer 20, error 0.38). No baseline or threshold is given, and the paper says the coherence of reconstructed outputs roughly matches clean outputs (Fig. 7).

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Measured normalized latent reconstruction error for SAE reconstruction without intervention.
rows.note: The paper says reconstruction errors vary across models and identifies GPT2-small SAEs as an exception to the generally consistent errors.
rows.check: An error of 1.64 is worse than a zero reconstruction, so it may reflect an SAE/hook mismatch rather than SAE incompleteness. The authors flag it as an exception without explaining it, so treat it with caution.

rows.subject: SAEs (aggregate across evaluated models)
rows.operation_detail: Intervened on SAE features for the ten simple word- or phrase-related topics and measured intervention success rate against normalized latent edit distance.

conditions.value: aggregate; individual SAE results not stated in the text

rows.measure: Intervention success rate as a function of normalized latent edit distance
rows.note: The text says SAEs require significantly larger edits for reasonable success and attributes their lower performance in general to noise in feature labels. Numerical curve values are not stated.
rows.check: Success rates depend on Neuronpedia auto-interp labels; the authors attribute SAE underperformance to label noise. This measures label-based steering efficacy, not whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units. The row also mixes SAEs from different models and gives figure-only values.

rows.subject: SAEs (aggregate across evaluated models)
rows.operation_detail: Intervened on features corresponding to the selected topics and measured probability assigned to related tokens.

conditions.value: intervention topics; individual SAE conditions not stated
aggregate; individual SAE results not stated in the text

rows.note: The authors state that all methods across models increase intervention-related token probability, even when output intervention does not succeed; SAE probabilities are around 10e−5, compared with 10e−4 to 0.5 for the other methods.
rows.check: Intervened token probability for labelled SAE features is a steering metric, not a measure of whether SAE features are the model's units. The value '10e-5' is an approximate magnitude read from Fig. 10, aggregated across models.

relationships.reason: Normalized reconstruction error is 0.38 (r1), so the SAE does not fully reconstruct activations, though reconstructed outputs keep near-clean coherence (Fig. 7).
relationships.display_finding: Normalized reconstruction error was 0.38, so activations were not fully reconstructed, though reconstructed outputs kept near-clean coherence.

relationships.reason: Normalized reconstruction error is 1.64 (r2), far from complete reconstruction. The authors note it as an exception, and a possible setup artifact is not ruled out.
relationships.display_finding: Normalized reconstruction error was 1.64; the authors note this as an exception, and a setup artifact is not ruled out.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: SAE reconstructions are not exact, intervention success is lower and requires larger edits, and the authors report errors in post-hoc feature labels; these results qualify the reliability and completeness of SAE features without testing their stability or canonicality. Rows r1–r4.
